why: The seam between the browser client and ui.js, pinned from BOTH sides against these literals.
The frontend suite stubs fetch and the node suite drives a real socket, so neither can
see the two disagreeing: the client could build /api/projects/x/behaviour/ID/steps
(singular) and both suites would stay green — one over its own stub, the other over its
own hand-typed path. A green suite over a mock proves the mock.
So the paths and bodies below are written down ONCE. client.test.ts asserts the client
emits exactly these; kit.test.js feeds exactly these to a running ui.js and asserts the
file on disk changed. Drift on either side turns one of them red.

corpus.gamma.beh:
# a comment that must survive
behaviour BEH-G "gamma"
  actor engineer
  when opens page:Home
  then sees region:Shared
corpus.two words.beh:
behaviour BEH-W "spaced"
  actor engineer
  when opens page:Home
corpus.delta.beh:
# delta carries the one thing gamma cannot: a machine's inference,
# included but marked unreviewed per claude-code-bot#68. Adjudicating it is
# the only write in Kit that CHANGES a line instead of adding one.
behaviour BEH-D "delta"
  actor engineer
  source inferred tests/DeltaTests.cs:It_works
  review unreviewed
  when opens page:Home
corpus.epsilon.beh:
# epsilon exists to make the GLOBAL noun namespace visible in the contract.
# It shares region:Shared with gamma and nothing else, so binding that noun
# must report epsilon back — and binding button:Solo must report nobody.
behaviour BEH-E "epsilon"
  actor engineer
  then sees region:Shared

_comment: Seed bindings for the contract. page:Home is ALREADY BOUND, so the rebind refusal has something to refuse.

requests.what: add one step to a behaviour that exists
add a whole new behaviour, actor included
an app name that has to survive the URL, and a behaviour id that does too
a step the grammar refuses — the corpus must be untouched and the reason must travel
approve an inference — the review line is REPLACED, not appended beside the old one
deny it instead, with the correction his #68 requires

args: the page is Dashboard, not Home

body.note: the page is Dashboard, not Home

expect.fileMustMatch: review denied the page is Dashboard, not Home

requests.what: a bare denial is refused by the parser's own rule — a denial with no correction deletes a line
a note carrying a newline could splice a line into the TARGET, which rule 3 exempts
bind a noun — the write that lands in bindings.json, not in this app's corpus
binding a noun ANOTHER corpus also uses says so — the namespace is global
rebinding a noun that is already bound is refused — it would change every corpus that mentions it
